issues.legal_issue: A written statement made by a mortgagor in context may acknowledge a mortgagee’s subsisting right and renew the limitation period when it admits their jural relationship.
material_facts: The mortgagor had granted mortgage security to the mortgagee, and their only subsisting relationship when the letter was written was that of mortgagor and mortgagee.
After the mortgagor had earlier asked the mortgagee to prevent a sale by a prior mortgagee, and the mortgagee had paid money to avert that sale, the property was again advertised for sale.
The mortgagor wrote and signed a letter referring to the mortgagee as interested, inviting him to take up the whole, and stating that a payment would stop the sale.
Read in that context, the letter referred to the mortgagee’s interest as a puisne mortgagee and acknowledged the mortgage relationship before the relevant limitation period expired.
issues.conclusion: The letter was a valid acknowledgment of the mortgagee’s right under section 19 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, and a fresh limitation period ran from the acknowledgment; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 19 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, a written and signed acknowledgment made before expiry of limitation in respect of the right claimed starts a fresh limitation period. It must relate to a subsisting liability and the words, read in their context and with surrounding circumstances, must indicate and be intended expressly or impliedly to admit the parties’ jural relationship. The precise nature of the right need not be specified, and no promise to pay is necessary; the acknowledgment does not create a new cause of action. The Court relied on Green v. Humphreys (1884) 26 Ch. D. 474; Beti Maharani v. Collector of Etawah (1894) L.R. 22 I.A. 31; Sukhamoni Chowdhrani v. Ishan Chunder Roy (1897) L.R. 25 I.A. 95; Munshi Lal v. Hira Lal, I.L.R. [1947] All. 11; and Swaminatha Odayar v. Subbarama Ayyar (1927) I.L.R. 50 Mad. 548. It distinguished Dharma Vithal v. Govind Sadvalkar (1881) I.L.R. 8 Bom. 99, where the writing did not itself admit the relevant jural relationship.

rule.if: limitation_suit and written_signed_statement and statement_before_limitation_expiry and relates_to_subsisting_liability and admits_jural_relationship and maker_intended_admission

predicates.limitation_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking to enforce a right for which the applicable limitation period matters.
predicates.written_signed_statement: The person against whom the right is claimed makes a written statement and signs it.
predicates.statement_before_limitation_expiry: The person makes the statement before the limitation period for the claim has expired.
predicates.relates_to_subsisting_liability: The statement concerns a liability that still exists when the person makes it.
predicates.admits_jural_relationship: The statement, read in context, indicates the existing legal relationship between the person making it and the person claiming the right.
predicates.maker_intended_admission: The words and circumstances show that the person making the statement intended expressly or impliedly to admit that relationship.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a suit and the other person makes a timely, signed written statement that concerns a subsisting liability and is intended to admit their legal relationship, the statement restarts limitation.
